system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and reviewer note are advocacy, not agreed terms. None should be treated as cleared without Buyer confirmation. The disclosure letter identifies several unresolved matters but does not establish that they have been cured.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher cap—seek **100% of price**, with a negotiated fallback no lower than **50%**. | **Reject 20%:** it leaves Buyer bearing substantial undisclosed-loss risk on a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 per claim; AUD 250,000 **deductible** basket. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims, and a **tipping** basket (all qualifying loss recoverable once crossed). | **Counter:** the proposed structure can exclude numerous real losses and the first AUD 250,000 of recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notice within 18 months; default time limit for all Claims. | At least **24–36 months** for general warranties, with distinct longer periods for tax, title, IP and indemnities; timely notified claims survive resolution. | **Reject the universal 18-month limit:** some liabilities emerge only after a full operating or audit cycle. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Same cap and period as general warranties. | Separate fundamental/title warranties, surviving at least **six years**, with liability up to the **full purchase price** (and no general basket or de minimis). | **Reject parity:** Buyer must have robust recourse if Seller cannot transfer the shares and title promised. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance terms apply to **all Claims**. | Express carve-out for fraud, dishonesty and deliberate concealment from **every** cap, threshold, time limit, knowledge/disclosure bar and exclusive-remedy provision. | **Insist:** Seller must not use contractual limitations to shield intentional wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Wholesale disclosure of data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only **specific, fair disclosures** that identify the nature and reasonably ascertainable scope of an exception against the relevant warranty; no deemed disclosure by mere document availability. | **Reject blanket disclosure:** a data dump should not silently neutralise warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer/advisers or discoverable in data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier; if unavoidable, confine it to **actual, conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals**, not advisers or constructive knowledge. | **Reject discoverability:** it transfers Seller’s warranty risk to Buyer’s diligence process. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on written consent. Final consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions are not evidenced. | A non-waivable-by-Seller **Completion condition** for effective written consent **and satisfaction of all attached conditions**, in form acceptable to Buyer; termination right if unmet. | **Do not close on efforts alone:** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release after Completion. | Repayment from Seller proceeds **at or before Completion**, debt-free price adjustment, and bank payoff/release documents and security-discharge mechanics delivered at Completion. | **Reject an unsecured post-Completion promise:** Buyer should not inherit the debt or its security risk. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow. | Identify payer and timing; treat bonuses **and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs** as Seller-funded or deduct them from price; evidence in funds flow. | **Require an adjustment:** the obligation is transaction-triggered and presently unpriced. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 shown open, without payment or assignment evidence. | Before Completion, obtain cleared-payment evidence and confirmatory assignment; retain a **separate indemnity** for resulting title, use, infringement and remediation losses, not merely the fee. | **Broaden protection:** paying AUD 180,000 may not by itself cure an IP ownership defect. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary, not expected material; access, scope and notification duty unresolved. | Completion-stage investigation, preservation and remediation covenants, legal notification assessment, prompt updates, and a **specific indemnity/holdback** for pre-Completion incident losses. | **Keep it open:** uncertainty is not proof of a breach, but neither is it proof of no exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate described as ordinary-course cost. | Review all three together for execution, timing, termination and accrued liability; prohibit new commitments without consent and allocate pre-Completion or transaction-driven costs to Seller. | **Do not accept the label:** the record does not establish that these commitments are unavoidable or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | One limitation, remedy and reliance regime for Claims of any nature. | Expressly separate general warranties from fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, debt/price adjustments, covenants and fraud; specify applicable cap and survival for each, subject to no double recovery. | **Redraft the architecture:** an “all Claims” default can erase negotiated special protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | DD-012 share register shows Seller holds 100%. | Verify issued capital, options/convertibles, beneficial ownership, encumbrances, constitution, corporate authorities and PPSR position; obtain transfer instruments and clean-title deliverables. | **Do not rely on the register alone:** it does not establish unencumbered, fully transferable title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Specific tax and IP warranties, appropriately long survival, separate caps/indemnities for identified exposures, and clear treatment of pre-Completion tax and IP chain of title. | **Reopen both:** their risk profile and discovery periods differ from ordinary operating warranties. |

**Priority for the mark-up:** make Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, title delivery and the Ironquay cure true Completion deliverables; then fix the disclosure and limitation architecture so those protections are not inadvertently overridden.
=== END ADVICE ===
